items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VII, List of Answers on Terminology 15:1
items.html: When the vessel is no longer fit to receive anything at all from the light of Atzilut, it is completely nullified from where it stands, and the vessel is considered broken. But when it is still fit to receive from the degree of Atzilut, though only from a place lower than itself, and it cannot receive from the upper light that belongs to its own degree, then the vessel is considered nullified. That is, it does not function in its proper place, and that vessel is nullified from within the degree, but the vessel is not completely broken, since it still receives light — and although it is below its own level, it is still a reception. (p. 487, Item 4)
